messages.subject: finding efficient samplers
parts:
Hi all,
Running the model reported below I found difficulties in finding efficient samplers for some parameters. I made some trials, most of them randomly (trials and related effective sample sizes reported below model script). I wonder how I can improve mixing for the worse-sampled parameters and in which way I can understand what sampler combinations are more effective. Data are not reported, since I am more interested in the strategy I can use to find the best samplers. In this case mixing is poor or absent for two parameters in the probability scale (mean.phi and mean.p) and one in the log scale (mu.rho) Any advice would be greatly appreciated.
Thanks,
Simone

######MODEL:
library(nimble)
library(coda)

DDCode <-  nimbleCode({
  n1 ~ dunif(0,170)
  N[1] ~ dpois(n1)
  rho1 ~ T(dnorm(1,0.01),0,)
  rho[1] <- rho1
  N[2] ~ dpois(N[1] * rho[1])
  lP[1] <- log(N[1]/N[2])
  for (t in 2:(s-1)){
    A[t-1] ~ dbin(phi[t],N[t])
    B[t-1] ~ dnegbin(gamma_constr[t+1],A[t-1])
    N[t+1] <- A[t-1]+B[t-1]
    lP[t] <- log(N[t]/N[2])
  }

    phi[s] <- 0
    for (t in 1:(s-1)){
      phi[t] <- 1 / (1 + exp(-logit.phi[t]))
      logit.phi[t] <- mu.phi + eps.phi[t]
      eps.phi[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.phi)
    }
    mu.phi <- log(mean.phi / (1-mean.phi))
    mean.phi ~ dunif(0,1)
    tau.phi <- 1 / (sigma.phi * sigma.phi)
    sigma.phi ~ dunif(0, 5)

    for (t in 2:(s-1)){
      rho[t] <- exp(log.rho[t])
      log.rho[t] <- mu.rho + eps.rho[t]
      eps.rho[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.rho)
    }
    mu.rho ~ dnorm(0, 0.1)
    mean.rho <- exp(mu.rho)
    tau.rho <- 1 / (sigma.rho * sigma.rho)
    sigma.rho ~ dunif(0, 2)

    for (t in 1:s){
      p[t] <- 1 / (1 + exp(-logit.p[t]))
      logit.p[t] <- mu.p + eps.p[t]
      eps.p[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.p)

      mu[t] ~ dunif(0,1)
    }
    mu.p <- log(mean.p / (1-mean.p))
    mean.p ~ dunif(0,1)
    tau.p <- 1 / (sigma.p * sigma.p)
    sigma.p ~ dunif(0, 5)

for (i in 1:(s-1)) {
    fec[i] <- rho[i]-phi[i]
}

    gamma[1] <- 0
    for (i in 2:s) {
      gamma[i] <- (phi[i-1] / rho[i-1])
      gamma_constr[i] <- min(gamma[i],1)
    }

    ########### (ZERO-TRICK) ######
    zeros ~ dpois(zero.mean)
    zero.mean <- -L + C
    L <- condL(phi=phi[1:11], rho=rho[1:11], gamma=gamma[1:11], p=p[1:12], mu=mu[1:12],
               u=u[1:12], n=n[1:12], v=v[1:12], d=d[1:12], s=s)
}
)


  #### conditional likelihood as a NIMBLE function  ####
  condL <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(phi = double(1), rho = double(1), gamma = double(1), p = double(1), mu =  double(1),
                   u = double(1), n = double(1), v = double(1), d = double(1), s = double()) {
      returnType(double(0))
 
      firstexpo <- numeric(length = s)
      secondexpo_a <- numeric(length = s)
      secondexpo_b <- numeric(length = s)
      secondexpo <- numeric(length = s)
      thirdexpo <- numeric(length = s-1)
      fourthexpo <- numeric(length = s)
      fifthexpo <- numeric(length = s)
      sixthexpo <- numeric(length = s)

      secondexpo_a[1] <- u[1]
      secondexpo_b[1] <- 0
      secondexpo[1] <- secondexpo_a[1] - secondexpo_b[1] - n[1]
      thirdexpo[1] <- sum(v[2:s])
      fourthexpo[1] <- n[1]-d[1]
      fifthexpo[1] <- sum(u[2:s])
      sixthexpo[1] <- v[1]-d[1]

      firstexpo[s] <- sum(u[1:(s-1)])
      secondexpo_a[s] <- sum(u[1:s])
      secondexpo_b[s] <- sum(v[1:(s-1)])
      secondexpo[s] <- secondexpo_a[s] - secondexpo_b[s] - n[s]
      fourthexpo[s] <- n[s]-d[s]
      fifthexpo[s] <- 0
      sixthexpo[s] <- v[s]-d[s]
     
      for (i in 2:(s-1)) {
        firstexpo[i] <- sum(u[1:(i-1)])
        secondexpo_a[i] <- sum(u[1:i])
        secondexpo_b[i] <- sum(v[1:(i-1)])
        secondexpo[i] <- secondexpo_a[i] - secondexpo_b[i] - n[i]
        thirdexpo[i] <- sum(v[(i+1):s])
        fourthexpo[i] <- n[i]-d[i]
        fifthexpo[i] <- sum(u[(i+1):s])
        sixthexpo[i] <- v[i]-d[i]
      }
      denom_expo <- sum(u[1:s])

      chi[s] <- 1

        xi.tmp[i] <- (1-gamma[i]) + (gamma[i] * ((1-p[i-1])/(1-(p[i-1] * (1-mu[i-1])))) * xi[i-1])
        xi[i] <- max(xi.tmp[i],0.00001)
      }
     
      for (i in 1:(s-1)) {
       
        chi[i] <- (1-phi[i]) + (phi[i] * (1-p[i+1]) * chi[i+1])
      }
     
     l.num[1] <- (u[1] * log(xi[1])) + (n[1] * log(p[1])) + (secondexpo[1] * log(1-p[1])) +
        (thirdexpo[1] * log(phi[1])) + (fourthexpo[1] * log(mu[1])) + (d[1] * log(1-mu[1])) + (fifthexpo[1] * log(1-(p[1]*(1-mu[1])))) +
        (sixthexpo[1] * log(chi[1]))

      l.num[s] <- (u[s] * log(xi[s])) + (firstexpo[s] * (log(phi[s-1]) - log(rho[s-1]))) + (n[s] * log(p[s])) + (secondexpo[s] * log(1-p[s])) +
        (fourthexpo[s] * log(mu[s])) + (d[s] * log(1-mu[s])) + (fifthexpo[s] * log(1-(p[s]*(1-mu[s])))) +
        (sixthexpo[s] * log(chi[s]))
     
      for (i in 2:(s-1)) {
        l.num[i] <- (u[i] * log(xi[i])) + (firstexpo[i] * (log(phi[i-1]) - log(rho[i-1]))) + (n[i] * log(p[i])) + (secondexpo[i] * log(1-p[i])) +
          (thirdexpo[i] * log(phi[i])) + (fourthexpo[i] * log(mu[i])) + (d[i] * log(1-mu[i])) + (fifthexpo[i] * log(1-(p[i]*(1-mu[i])))) +
          (sixthexpo[i] * log(chi[i]))
      }

      PROD1[1] <- 1
      for (j in 1:(s-1)){
        PROD1_tmp[1,j] <- 0
      }

      for (i in 2:(s-1)) {
        for (j in i:(s-1)){
          PROD1_tmp[i,j] <- 0
        }
      }
      for (i in 2:s) {
        for (j in 1:(i-1)){
          PROD1_tmp[i,j] <- phi[j] * (1-(p[j]*(1-mu[j])))
        }
      }
      PROD1[2] <- PROD1_tmp[2,1]
      for (i in 3:s) {
        PROD1[i] <- prod(PROD1_tmp[i,1:(i-1)])
      }

      PROD2[s] <- 1
      for (i in 1:(s-1)) {
        for (j in (i+1):s) {
          PROD2_tmp[i,j] <- gamma[j]
        }
      }

      for (i in 1:(s-1)) {
       
        for (j in 1:i) {
          PROD2_tmp[i,j] <- 0
        }
      }
      PROD2[s-1] <- PROD2_tmp[(s-1),s]
      for (i in 1:(s-2)) {
        PROD2[i] <- prod(PROD2_tmp[i,(i+1):s])
      }
      for (i in 1:s) {
        denom_base_tmp[i] <- xi[i] * PROD1[i] * PROD2[i] * p[i]
      }
      denom_base <- sum(denom_base_tmp[1:s])
     
      l.denom <- denom_expo * log(denom_base)
     
      return(sum(l.num[1:s]) - l.denom)
    }
  )

messages.subject: Re: finding efficient samplers
parts:
Hi Simone,

Others might be able to make some suggestions of samplers and blocking to use. I haven't taken the time to think carefully about your model structure, but I'll comment on the fact that you are getting an effective sample size of 0 for mean.phi and mu.rho. This suggests that no proposals for these parameters are being accepted. 

1) We often see such results when there are bad initial values for the MCMC. In particular, if the initial values are inconsistent with the model structure or each other. A simple example would be starting an MCMC with a variance component equal to 0. 

2) You might try what is called a centered parameterization:

logit.phi[t] ~ dnorm(mu.phi, tau.phi)

and similarly for mu.rho.  Often non-centered parameterization such as you have now where you add mu.phi and eps.phi.

3) If you check that initial values are ok and centering doesn't help, a next diagnosis step would be to try modifying the RW samplers for mean.phi and mu.rho to have much smaller initial proposal scales. As the scale decreases, the parameters should at least mix a little bit, though each step will be small.  You can do this by using something like "control = list(scale = 0.01)" in your addSampler().

4) Some side notes:

a) You are using prod() in your model, which can lead to numerical problems compared to using sum() on the log scale. In your case it may not be possible to work on the log scale for that part of the model, but it is possible use of prod() may cause problems.

b) In nimble, one doesn't really need the zeros trick. Instead one would generally write a user-defined distribution. But if it's working as is, it's fine.

-chris

      secondexpo <- numeric(length = s)
      thirdexpo <- numeric(length = s-1)
      fourthexpo <- numeric(length = s)
      fifthexpo <- numeric(length = s)
      sixthexpo <- numeric(length = s)

      secondexpo_a[1] <- u[1]
      secondexpo_b[1] <- 0
      secondexpo[1] <- secondexpo_a[1] - secondexpo_b[1] - n[1]
      thirdexpo[1] <- sum(v[2:s])
      fourthexpo[1] <- n[1]-d[1]
      fifthexpo[1] <- sum(u[2:s])
      sixthexpo[1] <- v[1]-d[1]

      firstexpo[s] <- sum(u[1:(s-1)])
      secondexpo_a[s] <- sum(u[1:s])
      secondexpo_b[s] <- sum(v[1:(s-1)])
      secondexpo[s] <- secondexpo_a[s] - secondexpo_b[s] - n[s]
      fourthexpo[s] <- n[s]-d[s]
      fifthexpo[s] <- 0
      sixthexpo[s] <- v[s]-d[s]
     
      for (i in 2:(s-1)) {
        firstexpo[i] <- sum(u[1:(i-1)])
        secondexpo_a[i] <- sum(u[1:i])
        secondexpo_b[i] <- sum(v[1:(i-1)])
        secondexpo[i] <- secondexpo_a[i] - secondexpo_b[i] - n[i]
        thirdexpo[i] <- sum(v[(i+1):s])
        fourthexpo[i] <- n[i]-d[i]
        fifthexpo[i] <- sum(u[(i+1):s])
        sixthexpo[i] <- v[i]-d[i]
      }
      denom_expo <- sum(u[1:s])
      xi <- numeric(length = s)
      xi.tmp <- numeric(length = s)
      chi <- numeric(length = s)
      l.num <- numeric(length = s)
      PROD1 <- numeric(length = s)
      PROD2 <- numeric(length = s)
      denom_base_tmp <- numeric(length = s)
      PROD1_tmp <- matrix(nrow = s, ncol = s)
      PROD2_tmp <- matrix(nrow = s, ncol = s)
      xi[1] <- 1
      chi[s] <- 1
      for (i in 2:s) {
        xi.tmp[i] <- (1-gamma[i]) + (gamma[i] * ((1-p[i-1])/(1-(p[i-1] * (1-mu[i-1])))) * xi[i-1])
        xi[i] <- max(xi.tmp[i],0.00001)
      }
     
      for (i in 1:(s-1)) {
       
        chi[i] <- (1-phi[i]) + (phi[i] * (1-p[i+1]) * chi[i+1])
      }
     
     l.num[1] <- (u[1] * log(xi[1])) + (n[1] * log(p[1])) + (secondexpo[1] * log(1-p[1])) +
        (thirdexpo[1] * log(phi[1])) + (fourthexpo[1] * log(mu[1])) + (d[1] * log(1-mu[1])) + (fifthexpo[1] * log(1-(p[1]*(1-mu[1])))) +
        (sixthexpo[1] * log(chi[1]))

      l.num[s] <- (u[s] * log(xi[s])) + (firstexpo[s] * (log(phi[s-1]) - log(rho[s-1]))) + (n[s] * log(p[s])) + (secondexpo[s] * log(1-p[s])) +
        (fourthexpo[s] * log(mu[s])) + (d[s] * log(1-mu[s])) + (fifthexpo[s] * log(1-(p[s]*(1-mu[s])))) +
        (sixthexpo[s] * log(chi[s]))
     
      for (i in 2:(s-1)) {
        l.num[i] <- (u[i] * log(xi[i])) + (firstexpo[i] * (log(phi[i-1]) - log(rho[i-1]))) + (n[i] * log(p[i])) + (secondexpo[i] * log(1-p[i])) +
          (thirdexpo[i] * log(phi[i])) + (fourthexpo[i] * log(mu[i])) + (d[i] * log(1-mu[i])) + (fifthexpo[i] * log(1-(p[i]*(1-mu[i])))) +
          (sixthexpo[i] * log(chi[i]))
      }

      PROD1[1] <- 1
      for (j in 1:(s-1)){
        PROD1_tmp[1,j] <- 0
      }

      for (i in 2:(s-1)) {
        for (j in i:(s-1)){
          PROD1_tmp[i,j] <- 0
        }
      }
      for (i in 2:s) {
        for (j in 1:(i-1)){
          PROD1_tmp[i,j] <- phi[j] * (1-(p[j]*(1-mu[j])))
        }
      }
      PROD1[2] <- PROD1_tmp[2,1]
      for (i in 3:s) {
        PROD1[i] <- prod(PROD1_tmp[i,1:(i-1)])
      }

      PROD2[s] <- 1
      for (i in 1:(s-1)) {
        for (j in (i+1):s) {
          PROD2_tmp[i,j] <- gamma[j]
        }
      }

      for (i in 1:(s-1)) {
       
        for (j in 1:i) {
          PROD2_tmp[i,j] <- 0
        }
      }
      PROD2[s-1] <- PROD2_tmp[(s-1),s]
      for (i in 1:(s-2)) {
        PROD2[i] <- prod(PROD2_tmp[i,(i+1):s])
      }
      for (i in 1:s) {
        denom_base_tmp[i] <- xi[i] * PROD1[i] * PROD2[i] * p[i]
      }
      denom_base <- sum(denom_base_tmp[1:s])
     
      l.denom <- denom_expo * log(denom_base)
     
      return(sum(l.num[1:s]) - l.denom)
    }
  )
